newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ share index edges lower, corp results dominates.
newsitem.headline: NZ share index edges lower, corp results dominates.

text.p: New Zealand's top 40 share market index ended marginally lower on Wednesday in a market dominated by corporate results.
The index closed 1.96 lower at 2,329.35 on light volume of ND$41.7 million.

While the index remains fairly static, individual stocks were quite volatile. Telecom still dominates and it ended eight cents down at $6.87 ahead of the start of the company's $1 billion share buyback due to start very soon.
County Natwest broker Sean Vaughan said there were some nervous sellers waiting for the start of the buyback.
Air New Zealand's sharply lower half year result was largely within expectations. The B shares responded by rising six cents to $3.93 on good volume but the A shares fell four to $2.81.
Brokers said there were some questions about the quality of the result, notably the tax situation, but the presentation by the company portrayed a better picture than some expected.
Natural Gas Corp remained unchanged after its half year result.
Fletcher Building lost early gains while Fletcher Paper gained three cents despite weakness in the paper sector on Wall Street.
Among the other leaders, Brierley was two up at $1.39 and Carter Holt Harvey was one down at $3.29 amid speculation it may be on the verge of a large timber products company purchase in Australia.
